summary.short: Slovenian statute implementing the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689). Designates market surveillance and notifying authorities, creates a national AI ethics council and regulatory sandboxes, requires public-sector AI systems to be published, and sets misdemeanour fines for providers, deployers, importers, distributors, representatives and notified bodies. In force 15 days after publication.
summary.long: The Act implements Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) in Slovenia and sets national enforcement arrangements. The ministry for the information society is notifying authority for certain high-risk systems, and market surveillance is shared among the communications agency, the Information Commissioner, the Bank of Slovenia, the insurance supervision agency and the market inspectorate, each for defined areas. The communications agency is the single point of contact, coordinates a market surveillance council and must set up the first AI regulatory sandbox by 2 August 2026. It keeps a register of certain critical-infrastructure high-risk systems and requires public bodies to publish data on AI systems in use through a single information point. A five-member National Council for Ethics in AI is created. Misdemeanour fines apply to providers, deployers, importers, distributors, authorised representatives and notified bodies: base fines of EUR 25,000 to 250,000 (EUR 100,000 to 450,000 for large companies), with maxima of EUR 35 million or 7% of turnover for prohibited practices and lower tiers for other breaches. The Act enters into force fifteen days after publication.

notes: Source: Uradni list RS, št. 85/2025 (6.11.2025), as published (original text, not consolidated); the page also contains site text (cookie banner, index) that is not part of the Act. Internal inconsistency: Art. 29(3) and Art. 32(3) set the fine for the responsible person at 2.500 to 100.000 eur, while the parallel provisions (e.g., Art. 25(3), 30(3), 33(3), 34(3)) set 2.500 to 10.000 eur. Art. 2 defines terms by reference to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Several laws are referred to only generically (electronic communications, banking, insurance, inspection, misdemeanours, public procurement, classified information, business secrecy, archives) without citation, so no relation rows were created for them. The relation target_instrument_id fields are empty strings because no registry IDs were supplied.
